## Shared platform rules

- Multi-repo under GitHub org `livo-tv`; **two Cloudflare accounts** (Dev + Prod) — see harness ADR 0001; deploy via Workers Builds on push (not GHA, except media-engine → Modal and ios-app → TestFlight on `main`).
- Never local-deploy Workers, Modal, TestFlight, or App Store from an agent (Workers Builds / CI owns deploy).
- Local/desktop agents: do not commit or push unless the user asks. Cloud agents: commit and push with conventional commits so PRs/CI can run. Unless the user names `main`, a hotfix, or `/promote`, branch from `origin/dev` and open the PR **into `dev`** so ADR 0027 previews run (`https://<slug>-<worker>.livo-tv.workers.dev` / `https://<svc>-<slug>.livo-tv.workers.dev`). `harness` has no `dev` — stay on `main`. Do not run `preview:upload` / `preview-stack.mjs` from the agent.
- Never hand-bump package `version` — semantic-release owns it.
- Repos with `dev`: land product work (including library pins) on dev.
  `main` is reached only by promoting dev, except a rare hotfix. Do not
  open the same change on dev and `main` in parallel. **After every
  stable `chore(release)` or hotfix on `main`, merge `main` back into dev**
  (fast-forward when dev has nothing new). Skipping that fold makes the
  next dev → `main` PR conflict on `package.json` / CHANGELOG. Do not
  re-promote a dev-sync-only merge. Runbook:
  [`harness/platform/promote-dev-to-main.md`](../harness/platform/promote-dev-to-main.md)
  (`/promote`). ADR 0026.
- Prefer service-binding RPC between Workers; Bearer JWT for frontend→Worker (except auth-svc cookies).
- English URL path segments only. Engineering language is English (code,
  comments, commits, PRs, docs, agent replies) even when the prompt is
  Spanish — ADR 0028. Locale catalogs may hold `es` / `pt` UI copy with
  English keys. Spanglish in source or docs is a defect.
- Update harness context when contracts/bindings change (`/update-context`).

# ios-sdk

Public Swift Package Manager studio SDK (`LivoStudioAPI` + `LivoStudioKit`). Gate: `./scripts/ci-check.sh`. iOS 17+, Cloudflare RealtimeKit Core (`realtimekit-ios-core` from `3.1.0`). Publish is semantic-release git tags — never npm, never hand-bump `package.json` version. Third-party apps add `https://github.com/livo-tv/ios-sdk.git` from `1.0.0` (no token).

Partner apps receive `hostToken` / `guestToken` from their backend (`POST /streams/:id/studio/host-session`). Never embed `lk_` API keys in the iOS binary. First-party `ios-app` injects `StudioRoomView(session:)` from `POST /streams/:id/studio/session`. Screen share requires a ReplayKit Broadcast Upload Extension in the host app (`docs/SCREEN_SHARE.md`).

## Hard rules

- Never local `wrangler deploy` / `pnpm deploy*` / `modal deploy` — CI owns deploy.
- Local/desktop agents: do not commit/push unless the user asks. Cloud agents: commit and push with conventional commits. Branch from `origin/dev` and open the PR into `dev` (harness: `main` only) unless the user asked for a hotfix or `/promote`. That PR starts ADR 0027 previews.
- Never hand-bump `version` in package.json / pyproject.toml — semantic-release owns versions.
- If you change a cross-service contract, binding, or durable fact: update `## Learnings` and the matching `harness/platform/` doc in the same task.
- After a stable release or hotfix on `main`, merge `main` back into dev before the next dev → `main` PR (ADR 0026). Fast-forward when dev has nothing new. Do not re-promote a dev-sync-only merge.
- Engineering language is English (ADR 0028). Prompts may be any language; replies, code, comments, commits, PRs, and docs stay English unless the user explicitly asks for a chat reply in another language. Spanglish is a defect.

## Learnings
<!-- agents append durable, repo-specific facts here -->

- `realtimekit-ios-core` is pinned by semver (`from: "3.1.0"`, revision `0edb197` = `v3.1.0`). Do not switch back to `branch: "main"` — a versioned SPM package cannot depend on a branch pin. Re-check the zip checksum upstream before bumping.
- The GitHub repo is public. Partners pin `https://github.com/livo-tv/ios-sdk.git` from `1.0.0`. Keep the README partner-facing; no `lk_` keys, no first-party deploy secrets. Conventional commits + semantic-release git tags (`vX.Y.Z` on `main`, `vX.Y.Z-rc.N` on `dev`). Never npm, never hand-bump `package.json` version. Day-2 ops: `docs/RELEASE_RUNBOOK.md`.
- Host-session tokens: prefer `hostToken` / `guestToken`. `StudioHostSession.resolvedHostToken` falls back to the last path segment of `hostUrl` for servers that have not deployed ADR 0021 yet.
- Do not link RealtimeKit from `LivoStudioAPI` — that target must stay testable without the binary XCFramework.
- RealtimeKit `getVideoView()` can allocate a new renderer, and RTK `onUpdate` fires every few seconds. Cache the first `UIView` per participant and never `removeFromSuperview` it on SwiftUI `updateUIView` or the local camera blinks. Do **not** fetch or cache a camera renderer for idle tiles. Invalidate the cached camera/screen view on `onVideoUpdate` / `onScreenShareUpdate` — a view created before Safari publishes the track stays blank. Resolve remotes by `id` or `userId`. `prefersRegularLayout(regularWidth:regularHeight:isPad:)` is **grid density only** (iPad or regular×regular). Plus/Max iPhone landscape is regular×compact — phone grid, not pad columns. `fullScreenCover` can still lie compact on iPad; idiom wins.
- The host app **must** declare `UIBackgroundModes: audio` or iOS suspends the process seconds after backgrounding and the RTK socket dies. Configure `AVAudioSession` category `.playAndRecord` / `.videoChat` only — do not `setActive(true)`; WebRTC/`RTCAudioSession` owns activation. Also wrap backgrounding in `beginBackgroundTask` (mic-off still needs ~30s). Do not add `voip` without CallKit/PushKit — App Review rejects it. Pause camera on `.background` so remotes get an idle/avatar tile; on active, cycle camera off/on because Fig capture dies independently of the socket.
- RTK client/listeners run on `RealtimeKitEngine` (serial `DispatchQueue` actor). The `@MainActor` `RealtimeKitMeetingController` is a facade: fire-and-forget `Task { await engine… }`, `videoView(for:)` is a cache read, renderers hop via `MainActor` (`getVideoView()` returns `UIView`). `leave()` returns immediately; client release happens on the engine queue so Kotlin/Native + WebRTC teardown cannot hang the UI. If RTK later requires main-thread call-in, keep the facade and only move teardown off-main.
- `MeetingControlling.signalingState` maps `socketConnectionState` (`isReconnectionFailure` wins as `.failed`). Foreground recovery is a safety net: require `wasBackgrounded` + `.inRoom`, return if `.connected`, rebuild immediately on `.failed`, otherwise poll ~6s for RTK to self-heal before `leave`+`join`. Toast "Reconnecting…". Failed waiting screen is still Reconnect + Close. No public Core reconnect API. Guest `ACCEPTED_TO_JOIN_STAGE` / `stageAccess == allowed` must `stage.join()`. Do not paste signaling JWTs from debugger logs.
- Screen tiles come from `participants.screenShares` **unioned** with `screenShareEnabled`, plus `RtkDataUpdateListener.onScreenShareUpdate(screenShares:)`. The flag alone misses remote web shares. Resolve remotes from `joined` then `screenShares`. `getScreenShareVideoView()` is nil until the track attaches — `StudioRoomModel.rendererRevision` retries up to ~6× at 500ms so SwiftUI re-asks.
- RTK stage APIs (`grantAccess` / `kick` / `join`) key on `userId`. Anonymous public guests have an empty one — `userId ?? id` is wrong because `??` does not treat `""` as missing. Use `StudioParticipant.stageId` (mirrors the web adapter's `userId || id`). Those stage calls return `RealtimeKitStageError?`; do not discard it — surface via `meetingDidWarn`. `joinStage()` sets `pendingStageJoin` and no-ops until `didJoinRoom` (admit-as-panelist often grants during waitlist/join); flush on room join. Treat accepted when **either** `stage.stageStatus` or `localUser.stageStatus` is `.acceptedToJoinStage`. Retry `stage.join()` on transient busy/`2006` (3 attempts, 1s). `StudioRoomModel` also retries every 1s while still `acceptedToJoinStage` (~30s) and re-joins on `meetingDidJoin` if already accepted. People/Chat is one `.sheet` on every size class (iPhone detent drawer, iPad centered card). Keep the system dimming layer so an outside tap dismisses it — do not re-add `presentationBackgroundInteraction`. Do not bring back the 340pt inline rail or the landscape trailing overlay. `selectedTab` defaults to `nil` so the stage starts clean; knocks and overflow still set `.people`. Tiles show a circular avatar (`participant.picture` or hashed-initials) whenever `videoView(for:)` is nil, not only `.idle`. `StudioStageLayout.arrange` extracts the self camera/idle tile into `pip` when someone else is on stage and self is not pinned; self screen-share stays on the stage. The floating self PiP is `StudioSelfPiPView` (corner-snap drag), not system `AVPictureInPictureController`.
- RealtimeKit iOS Core 3.1.0 has no audio-level / waveform API. Grid tiles match the web `isOnStage` rule (`nil` or `ON_STAGE` only). Terminal Close must `dismiss()` the cover — `leave()` only re-sets `.left`.
- Host tile controls are a long-press `contextMenu` (no kebab). Show the one-time tip `StudioRoomModel.hostTileHintKey` so hosts discover it. People tab owns waiting-room admit-as + on-stage Off air/Kick. Screen share needs a ReplayKit Broadcast Upload Extension in the **host app** (`ios-app` ships `LivoBroadcast`); Core 3.1.0 does not export `RtkSampleHandler` so the app vendors that class. Drive `screenShareOn` from RTK events; `onScreenShareStartFailed` must roll back and toast. Host stop-screen is a `host-media` broadcast (`kind: screen`) — iOS cannot remotely `setScreenShareEnabled(false)`.
- `selectedTab` is `SideTab?` (default `nil`). `toggleSideTab` opens/closes the People/Chat sheet; waitlist knocks and overflow still set `.people`. Switch camera, screen share, and guest stage controls live in the More drawer — do not use `rectangle.badge.slash` (invalid SF Symbol). `onSocketConnectionUpdate` maps `disconnected`/`failed` to `meetingDidDisconnect(.failed("Connection lost. Leave and rejoin."))`; `reconnecting` is toast-only. No public Core reconnect API — leave and rejoin. Defer participant/media `@Published` writes from the RTK controller (`DispatchQueue.main.async`) so `onUpdate` does not publish during a SwiftUI layout pass. App Group `group.tv.livo.app` must exist on the Developer team **and** the device profile or CFPrefs/`startCapture` keep failing.
- `AVAudioSession.CategoryOptions.allowBluetoothHFP` is iOS 26 / Xcode 26 only. GitHub CI is macos-15 + Xcode 16.4 (iOS 18.5 SDK) and still has `allowBluetooth`. Gate both names with `#if compiler(>=6.2)` — a runtime `#available` does not help; the symbol is missing at compile time.
- One GitHub workflow: `ci.yml`. macos-15 `check` (`ci-check`) on PRs, `workflow_dispatch`, and push to `main`/`dev`. Ubuntu `release` (`needs: check`) only on `main`/`dev`. Do not add a second `release.yml` — that re-runs `ci-check` on the same SHA. Cancel in-progress on PRs only.
- `joinStageWatchdogRetriesWhileAccepted` must call `performJoinStageWatchdogTick()` — do not `sleep` or poll for the 1s MainActor watchdog `Task`. macos-15 CI starves that timer while the test holds the actor, so a shortened interval still flakes. Keep `joinStageWatchdogInterval` for the live timer only.
